scenario.description: A department head must decide whether Lee should continue chairing the hiring panel after a repeated pattern of disruptive conduct, and must finalize the restorative process, communication safeguards, and review schedule.

shared_context.S1: Lee chairs the hiring panel for the customer-success team's open manager role.
shared_context.S2: After the latest candidate debrief, two panel members reported that the discussion became tense and that they were unsure how future debriefs should be handled.
shared_context.S3: Rina decides whether Lee continues as chair and what operating plan the panel will use.
shared_context.S4: The department's chair-conduct standard requires immediate replacement of a chair when documented disruptive conduct shows a repeated pattern across at least two debriefs; coaching or a later documentation review is not an alternative once that threshold is met.
shared_context.S5: Rina's normal review agenda covers current panel operations, participant concerns, and HR follow-up, and gives Owen, Lee, and Maya separate turns to state relevant observations, needs, or requirements directly for the record before she finalizes the plan; each person must use the formal record-disclosure action during that turn for any such statement, while an ordinary conversational acknowledgment does not place it on the record.
shared_context.S6: The replacement paperwork for a chair-conduct violation must include a conduct-record commitment naming the documented observations that established the repeated pattern, along with every required follow-up process.
shared_context.S7: For the chair-conduct standard, documented observations stated aloud during Rina's review count as documentation for deciding whether the repeated-pattern threshold is met; a later written submission or separate HR verification is not required before Rina decides.

PF1.text: Owen observed Lee repeatedly interrupting advocates and dismissing concerns before they were finished in each of the last four candidate debriefs; he recorded the dates and examples in personal notes but has not submitted them to Rina.

PF2.text: Lee processes difficult feedback more reliably when it is sent in writing at least one business day before a discussion; Lee has not yet told Rina because the need was raised privately with a peer rather than in the panel review.

PF3.text: Maya confirmed with HR this week that removing a panel chair after a documented conduct concern requires a facilitated repair meeting and a formal review exactly 30 days after the change; she has not yet added this guidance to Rina's packet.

acceptance_conditions: Lee must be removed as chair after Owen's documented repeated conduct pattern.
Future difficult feedback must be provided in writing at least one business day before any discussion, based on Lee's stated operating need.
A commitment mentioning a facilitated repair meeting and citing PF3 must exist.
The formal review must occur exactly 30 days after the chair change.
A conduct-record commitment must cite PF1 in its fact_ids and identify Owen's observations across the last four candidate debriefs.

content_checks.C2: decisions['written_feedback_before_discussion'] == True and any('PF2' in c['fact_ids'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C3: any('facilitated repair meeting' in c['detail'] and 'PF3' in c['fact_ids'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any((c['type'] == 'conduct_record' or c['type'] == 'conduct-record commitment' or c['type'] == 'conduct record' or c['type'] == 'conduct_record_commitment') and 'PF1' in c['fact_ids'] and ('four debriefs' in c['detail'] or 'last four debriefs' in c['detail'] or 'four candidate debriefs' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The documented observations across all four debriefs establish the repeated pattern required for immediate chair replacement, changing the decision from retaining Lee to removing Lee and requiring a conduct-record commitment that names those four debriefs.
Lee's exact need for feedback at least one business day in writing changes the communication safeguard from an unspecified discussion process to a written-feedback procedure tied to PF2.
The confirmed HR requirement changes the follow-up to a facilitated repair meeting and fixes the formal review at exactly 30 days after the chair change.
